what: When should you reach for the advanced tools?
title: Advanced Chunking and Backends in delarr
text: basic workflow vignette("delarr-getting-started", package = "delarr") enough need lazy pipeline final collect(). vignette next step: understanding chunk plans, running several summaries one pass, streaming backends, checking whether optional parallel path behaves way expect. examples use one small dense matrix validate key claims code.
code: set.seed(11) mat <- matrix(   rnorm(96),   nrow = 12,   ncol = 8,   dimnames = list(paste0("sample_", 1:12), paste0("feature_", 1:8)) )

what: What will the execution plan do?
title: Advanced Chunking and Backends in delarr
text: explain() shows effective output shape, chunk axis, chosen chunk size, recorded operations optimization.
code: pipe <- delarr(mat)[, -1] |>   d_map(~ .x^2 + 1) |>   d_where(function(x) x > 1.25, fill = 0)  plan <- explain(pipe, chunk_size = 3L) plan #> <delarr_explain> in: 12x8  out: 12x7  #> ops: 2  chunks: 3 (cols=3)  #> plan: map -> where

what: How do you let delarr choose a chunk size?
title: Advanced Chunking and Backends in delarr
text: want hard-code chunk_size, can pass memory budget target_bytes.
code: adaptive_plan <- explain(pipe, target_bytes = 256) adaptive_plan #> <delarr_explain> in: 12x8  out: 12x7  #> ops: 2  chunks: 4 (cols=2)  #> plan: map -> where  adaptive_result <- collect(pipe, target_bytes = 256) dim(adaptive_result) #> [1] 12  7

what: How do you compute several summaries in one pass?
title: Advanced Chunking and Backends in delarr
text: d_reduce_many() runs several built-reducers together returns matrix outputs common length.
code: row_summary <- d_reduce_many(   delarr(mat),   fns = list(sum = sum, mean = mean, max = max),   dim = "rows",   chunk_size = 3L )  row_summary[1:4, , drop = FALSE] #>                 sum       mean       max #> sample_1 -0.8688508 -0.1086063 2.2616090 #> sample_2  3.5083317  0.4385415 2.3396931 #> sample_3 -2.9752109 -0.3719014 1.1194619 #> sample_4 -3.9809604 -0.4976200 0.5064512

title: Advanced Chunking and Backends in delarr
text: block_apply() useful want chunk-local summaries diagnostics without materializing whole array.
code: col_blocks <- block_apply(   delarr(mat),   margin = "cols",   size = 3L,   fn = function(block) colMeans(block) )  block_means <- unlist(col_blocks, use.names = FALSE) block_means #> [1] -0.28978420 -0.35858092 -0.45034884 -0.16311026  0.30973503  0.02181969 #> [7] -0.11859494 -0.06352597

title: Advanced Chunking and Backends in delarr

what: How do you stream a transformed matrix to disk?
title: Advanced Chunking and Backends in delarr
text: writer interface useful result still large enough want hold memory. HDF5 backend optional; chunks run hdf5r package installed.
code: X <- delarr_hdf5(tf_in, "X") scaled <- X |> d_scale(dim = "cols", center = TRUE, scale = TRUE) writer <- hdf5_writer(tf_out, "X_scaled", ncol = ncol(X), chunk = c(6L, 4L))  collect(scaled, into = writer, chunk_size = 4L) disk_result <- read_hdf5(tf_out, "X_scaled") rbind(   mean = round(colMeans(disk_result), 6),   sd = round(apply(disk_result, 2L, stats::sd), 6) ) #>      [,1] [,2] [,3] [,4] [,5] [,6] [,7] [,8] #> mean    0    0    0    0    0    0    0    0 #> sd      1    1    1    1    1    1    1    1

what: How do you use shared-memory workers?
title: Advanced Chunking and Backends in delarr
text: install optional shard package, collect_shard() can evaluate supported pipeline worker processes keeping underlying matrix shared memory.
code: shard_result <- delarr_shard(mat) |>   d_map(~ .x * 2) |>   d_reduce(sum, dim = "rows") |>   collect_shard(workers = 2L, chunk_size = 3L)  head(shard_result) #>   sample_1   sample_2   sample_3   sample_4   sample_5   sample_6  #> -1.7377015  7.0166635 -5.9504217 -7.9619208 -5.4479018  0.2611599

what: How do you profile a candidate pipeline?
title: Advanced Chunking and Backends in delarr
text: profile_collect() repeats collect() records elapsed time plus size realized output.
code: profile <- profile_collect(pipe, reps = 2L, chunk_size = 3L) profile #> <delarr_profile> reps: 2 min/median/max: 0.0000 / 0.0005 / 0.0010 sec  #> output size (bytes): 2568

title: Getting Started with delarr
text: delarr lets write matrix pipelines everything already memory deferring actual work collect(). matters source matrix lives disk, want avoid intermediate allocations, need stream result directly another backend. vignette covers one small lazy pipeline, one streaming write HDF5, one custom backend. chunk planning, profiling, optional shared-memory workers, see vignette("advanced", package = "delarr").

what: What does a lazy pipeline look like?
title: Getting Started with delarr
text: Nothing materialized yet. object still delarr, work recorded plan. row-centering, every row mean zero. printed value largest absolute row mean collection.
code: set.seed(1) mat <- matrix(   rnorm(24),   nrow = 6,   ncol = 4,   dimnames = list(paste0("sample_", 1:6), paste0("feature_", 1:4)) )  lazy_mean <- delarr(mat) |>   d_center(dim = "rows") |>   d_map(~ .x * 0.5) |>   d_reduce(mean, dim = "rows")  lazy_mean #> <delarr> 6 x 1 - ops: center(rows) -> map -> reduce(rows) row_summary <- collect(lazy_mean, chunk_size = 2L) max(abs(row_summary)) #> [1] 6.245005e-17

what: How do row and column vectors broadcast?
title: Getting Started with delarr
text: Scalars, row-sized vectors, column-sized vectors stay lazy . delarr infers whether vector broadcast across rows columns length. length-based inference works matrix non-square, nrow ncol distinct. square n--n matrix bare length-n vector ambiguous — length matches dimensions — delarr resolves tie row-aligned (one value per row, broadcast across columns). matches base R, matrix + vector recycles vector columns also aligns element row . delarr emits one-time warning point flag ambiguity: actually want column alignment square matrix express bare vector; pass explicit conformable matrix instead: Silence warning options(delarr.warn_ambiguous_broadcast = FALSE) confirmed row-aligned default intend.
code: row_bias <- c(-1, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4) col_scale <- c(1, 0.5, 2, 1.5)  broadcasted <- collect((delarr(mat) + row_bias) * col_scale, chunk_size = 2L) broadcasted[1:3, , drop = FALSE] #>           feature_1  feature_2 feature_3  feature_4 #> sample_1 -1.6264538 -0.2562855 -3.242481 -0.2681682 #> sample_2  0.1836433  0.3691624 -4.429400  0.8908520 #> sample_3  0.1643714  0.7878907  4.249862  2.8784661 sq <- matrix(1:9, 3, 3) biased <- delarr(sq) + c(10, 20, 30) #> Warning: Ambiguous broadcast: a length-3 vector against a square 3x3 #> matrix is interpreted as row-aligned (one value per row) ... collect(biased) collect(delarr(sq) + matrix(c(10, 20, 30), 3, 3, byrow = TRUE))

what: How do you stream a result to HDF5?
title: Getting Started with delarr
text: delarr_hdf5() reads dataset lazily, hdf5_writer() lets stream transformed result back disk without materializing full output matrix R. HDF5 backend optional: install hdf5r package enable . code runs hdf5r available.
code: X <- delarr_hdf5(tf_in, "X") writer <- hdf5_writer(tf_out, "X_z", ncol = ncol(X), chunk = c(5L, 3L))  collect(X |> d_zscore(dim = "cols"), into = writer, chunk_size = 3L) z <- read_hdf5(tf_out, "X_z") rbind(   mean = round(colMeans(z), 6),   sd = round(apply(z, 2L, stats::sd), 6) ) #>      [,1] [,2] [,3] [,4] [,5] [,6] #> mean    0    0    0    0    0    0 #> sd      1    1    1    1    1    1

what: How do you wrap your own storage layer?
title: Getting Started with delarr
text: custom backend needs matrix dimensions pull() function can return arbitrary row column slices. backing store just another matrix, pattern works databases, APIs, memory-mapped files.
code: custom <- delarr_backend(   nrow = nrow(source_mat),   ncol = ncol(source_mat),   pull = function(rows = NULL, cols = NULL) {     if (is.null(rows)) rows <- seq_len(nrow(source_mat))     if (is.null(cols)) cols <- seq_len(ncol(source_mat))     source_mat[rows, cols, drop = FALSE]   },   dimnames = dimnames(source_mat) )  custom_result <- custom[1:4, 2:5] |>   d_map(~ .x^2) |>   collect(chunk_size = 2L)  custom_result #>       col_2 col_3 col_4 col_5 #> row_1   121   441   961  1681 #> row_2   144   484  1024  1764 #> row_3   169   529  1089  1849 #> row_4   196   576  1156  1936

what: Lazy Delayed Arrays with Fused Execution
title: Lazy Delayed Arrays with Fused Execution
text: delarr provides lightweight delayed array type R tidy-friendly API. keeps surface area small—one S3 class plus handful verbs—offering fused elementwise transforms, reductions, streamed materialisation. package supports ordinary 2D matrices N-dimensional arrays length(dim(x)) >= 2. Streamed results can also written straight disk via bundled HDF5 writer.

title: Lazy Delayed Arrays with Fused Execution

code: # install.packages("pkgload") pkgload::load_all(".")

code: library(delarr)  mat <- matrix(rnorm(20), 5, 4) arr <- delarr(mat)  # Lazy pipeline out <- arr |>   d_center(dim = "rows", na.rm = TRUE) |>   d_map(~ .x * 0.5) |>   d_reduce(mean, dim = "rows")  collect(out)

text: delarr limited matrices. -memory arrays HDF5 datasets 3 dimensions supported .
code: library(delarr)  x <- array(rnorm(3 * 4 * 5), dim = c(3, 4, 5))  # Slice lazily and operate along an explicit axis out <- delarr(x) |>   d_center(axis = 3L) |>   d_reduce(mean, axis = 3L)  dim(collect(out)) #> [1] 3 4

title: Lazy Delayed Arrays with Fused Execution
code: # assume `X` lives inside an HDF5 file lzy <- delarr_hdf5("input.h5", "X")  # Apply a transformation lazily and stream the result into a new dataset # (dim(lzy)[2] supplies the total column count for the writer) lzy |>   d_zscore(dim = "cols") |>   collect(into = hdf5_writer(     path = "output.h5",     dataset = "X_zscore",     ncol = dim(lzy)[2],     chunk = c(128L, 4096L)   ))

title: Lazy Delayed Arrays with Fused Execution
text: delarr_mem() wraps -memory matrix array least 2 dimensions. delarr_hdf5() exposes dataset hdf5r, including N-dimensional datasets. delarr_mmap() streams 2D matrices memory-mapped binary file via mmap package. delarr_backend() lets create seed (rows, cols) -> matrix pull function. hdf5_writer() pairs collect(= ...) stream results back disk without materialising full matrix memory (supply ncol size destination dataset front). core package depends rlang. hdf5r mmap backends optional: live Suggests, relevant constructors raise informative error package installed. can also add new backends via delarr_backend() without taking extra dependency.

title: Lazy Delayed Arrays with Fused Execution
text: d_map()/d_map2() elementwise transformations. d_center()/d_scale()/d_zscore()/d_detrend() common preprocessing, optional na.rm handling. N-d arrays, use axis =. d_reduce() row-wise column-wise reductions, explicit axis-based reductions N-d arrays, streaming na.rm support sum/mean/min/max. d_where() masked updates, optionally replacing masked entries via fill argument. collect() realise data (streamed chunks), optionally writing disk hdf5_writer(), block_apply() chunk-wise computation. d_aperm() lazy dimension permutation N-d arrays. verbs return another delarr, pipelines stay lazy collect() materialises result.

title: Lazy Delayed Arrays with Fused Execution
text: test suite exercises core class, slicing, verb fusion, reductions, chunk-aware execution, HDF5 streaming writer. Run locally :
code: pkgload::load_all(".") testthat::test_dir("tests/testthat")

title: Lazy Delayed Arrays with Fused Execution
text: core abstraction stable: -memory, HDF5, memory-mapped backends, fused verb pipeline, chunk-aware collect(), streaming HDF5 writer, lazy matrix products (d_matmul()) implemented, documented, tested. Two vignettes (vignette("delarr-getting-started") vignette("advanced")) cover workflow end end, benchmark scripts live notes/. Possible future directions, none required current use: Optional sparse-matrix adapters, backend can return sparse blocks without forcing dense. Writer-style = targets N-dimensional collect() (currently supported 2D output via custom = function(...) callbacks). Promoting notes/ benchmarks dedicated performance article.

title: delarr (development version)
text: Broadcasting bare length-n vector square n--n matrix ambiguous (length matches dimensions). delarr continues resolve row-aligned (one value per row, matching base R recycling), now emits warning operation-construction time choice explicit. Pass conformable matrix (e.g. matrix(v, n, n, byrow = TRUE)) column alignment. Silence warning options(delarr.warn_ambiguous_broadcast = FALSE).

title: delarr 0.1.0
text: First public release.

title: delarr 0.1.0
text: Lazy delarr arrays fused, chunk-aware execution engine. Pipelined verbs: d_map(), d_map2(), d_center(), d_scale(), d_zscore(), d_detrend(), d_reduce(), d_where(), d_aperm(), stay lazy collect(). Lazy, block-aware matrix products via d_matmul(). Storage backends: delarr_mem() (-memory matrices N-d arrays), delarr_hdf5() (HDF5 datasets, including N-d), delarr_mmap() (memory-mapped 2D matrices), delarr_backend() custom pull functions. Streaming output disk hdf5_writer() collect(= ...). block_apply() chunk-wise computation. Getting-started advanced vignettes plus benchmark scripts notes/.
